# GUI state model — the surface × field matrix

**Session:** S07 · **Generated by:** `harness/gui_field_extract.py` · **Pi used:** no
**Companion:** `GUI-INVENTORY.md` (the surfaces) · **Feeds:** ADR-001 (S08)

---

## 1. The headline: there is already one state model

KICKOFF §7 asks whether the surfaces should be generated "the same way". For **state**,
they already are.

```
                    redis (cp_controls)  ssd_monitor  Utils/psutil  cinepi_controller
                            \                |            |              /
                             \               |            |             /
                          simple_gui.populate_values()  -- 68 fields --
                             /                                    \
                    draw_gui()                             emit gui_data_change
                   PIL -> /dev/fb0                        Socket.IO -> browser
                   (surface 1)                                 (surface 2)
```

`app/main/events.py:57` — `initial_values.update(simple_gui.populate_values())`.
`app/main/routes.py:29-32` says so in a comment. Surface 2 has **no field set of its own**.

**So the operator's hypothesis is half right, and the half that is right is the expensive
half.** Deriving the surfaces "the same way" does not require building a shared state
model. It exists, it is 68 fields wide, and it has one owner. What is duplicated is
presentation: colours (F-007), labels (F-214), and layout.

Surfaces 3 and 4 are **not** on this bus at all, by design — see §5.

## 3. Source of truth, per provider class

| provider | count | source of truth | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `redis` | 14 | the `cp_controls` bus, read through `RedisController`'s **cache** | `get_value()` never touches redis; it reads the cache the `_listen` thread maintains. If that thread dies the values freeze silently (F-204). |
| `derived` | 21 | computed inside `populate_values` from redis values, `ssd_monitor`, `cinepi_controller` attributes and locals | Formatting logic lives with the field, not with the renderer — which is why surface 2 gets formatted strings, not raw values. |
| `literal` | 15 | inline string constants in `populate_values` | Ten of these are label text duplicated into the HTML (F-214). |
| `gui-internal` | 15 | `SimpleGUI` instance state (VU smoothing, lock flags, badges, display geometry) | Not on the redis bus. Surface 2 can only get these *because* it consumes `populate_values()`. |
| `slow-poll` | 2 | `_refresh_slow_values()` on a timer | `cpu_load`, `cpu_temp`. |
| `host` | 1 | `Utils.memory_usage` | `ram_load`. |

The `gui-internal` class is the interesting one for ADR-001: **15 of 68 fields are not
recoverable from redis.** Any option that renders a surface without going through
`SimpleGUI` has to reproduce them or lose them.

---

## 4. Where the surfaces genuinely differ

Twenty fields do not reach the web template. They are not twenty accidents:

| group | fields | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Labels | `iso_label`, `shutter_label`, `fps_label`, `wb_label`, `res_label`, `exposure_label`, `cpu_label`, `cpu_temp_label`, `ram_label`, `media_label`, `raw` | **Accidental duplication.** The strings are re-typed as HTML text nodes and currently agree exactly (F-214). One edit from drift. |
| Recording integrity counts | `drop_frame_count`, `drop_frame_live`, `drop_frame_during_last_take`, `tc_hole_count`, `missing_frame_count`, `frames_in_sync` | **Real capability difference.** The web GUI renders DROP and SYNC *badges* from the latched booleans but shows no counts (F-211). A deliberate choice or an omission — worth asking the operator. |
| Other | `color_temp_libcamera`, `disk_label`, `frame_count` | Mixed; `frame_count` is shown on HDMI during a take and absent from the browser. |

Everything else the HDMI GUI knows, the browser is already told.

---

## 5. Surfaces 3 and 4 are on different state models — correctly

| surface | state model | source of truth |
|---|---|---|
| 1 HDMI | `populate_values()` — 68 live fields | redis cache + GUI internals |
| 2 Web | **the same dict** | as above |
| 3 Settings editor | `settings.jsonc` + `/boot/firmware/config.txt` + a take listing | files on disk |
| 4 Recovery console | the same two files, plus systemd state and the journal | files on disk + `systemctl` |

Surfaces 3 and 4 edit **configuration**; 1 and 2 display **live state**. They are different
kinds of thing and unifying their state models would be a category error. The only shared
concern is that 3 and 4 both write `settings.jsonc` and `config.txt` — and there, both go
through validation ladders rather than raw writes.

### The settings editor's third state model — the action catalogue

Beyond the files, surface 3 carries a catalogue of controller method names. It exists three
times (46 / 46 / 94), the two hand-maintained copies agree perfectly *including on the same
wrong entry* (`set_log`), and the endpoint that would catch it has zero consumers
(F-218, F-219, F-220). This is the one place where surface 3 does hold duplicated live
truth, and it is already broken.

---

## 6. What this means for ADR-001

Stated as inputs, not as the decision — S08 makes the call, and PI-009 still blocks it.

**The cost of option C is lower than KICKOFF assumes.** Its two hard parts are a shared
state model and a widget/grouping spec. The state model exists (§1). A grouping spec with
labels, ordered items, per-item formatters and visibility conditions exists too, in
`setup_resources`' `left_section_layout` / `right_section_layout` (F-215). Both need
lifting out of `simple_gui.py`, not inventing.

**The cost of option B is lower than its value.** Tokens for colours and labels would kill
F-007 and F-214 — but F-215 says the project has already gone further than B on its own.
Shipping B would be stopping short of where the code already is.

**The residual hard problem is layout, and only layout.** `self.layout` is absolute
1920-reference pixel positions scaled by `shrink_x`/`shrink_y` (F-008). It scales; it does
not reflow. No amount of shared state fixes that, and it is the whole of the
immediate-mode/retained-mode tension in KICKOFF §7.

**Three constraints answered from source, no Pi needed:**
- *Constraint 2 (composition).* cinepi-raw binds its preview to the display at process
  start and cannot rebind — that is why HDMI hot-plug triggers a full capture restart
  (F-223). Options D and E must own that behaviour.
- *Constraint 5 (failure mode).* For the status quo, the honest answer is bad: if the redis
  `_listen` thread dies — which one raising subscriber does, silently (F-204) — every
  surface keeps displaying plausible frozen values. No surface shows an error. Any option
  must be scored against this, and the baseline is worse than it looks.
- *Scope.* Surface 4 must be excluded from any unification. Its value is its isolation
  (F-221).

**And one precedent to lean on:** control flow was already de-duplicated across web, CLI
and serial by routing everything through `POST /api/v1/cmd`, with the reason recorded in
the code (F-206). The project has done this exact kind of unification once and it held.
State and presentation are the two that did not get the same treatment.

---

## 7. Confidence and limits

Reproduce with `python3 system-review/harness/gui_field_extract.py --repo .`.

- **68 is a lower bound.** Dynamically named fields are invisible to an AST scan.
- **`web ✓` is a name match**, not proof of rendering. `web —` is the stronger signal.
- **`provider` is coarse** and `derived` is a genuine "not analysed", not a claim.
- **Nothing here was observed running.** No cadence, no frame timing, no composition
  behaviour. PI-009 remains the blocker for ADR-001 constraint 2, and F-223 narrows it
  without settling it.
- An earlier revision of the extractor counted 93 "fields" by walking every dict inside
  `populate_values`, including a nested colour table. It reported `normal`, `lock` and
  `low_voltage` as GUI fields. Two of those turned out to be real `values[...]` stores and
  one did not. The script now reads only the `values` binding. Treat any count in this
  review that was not produced by a committed script as provisional.
